column3: “He is a son of death” is rendered “he must surely die.”
“It had been determined from his father” is rendered “his father had decided.”
“Heat of anger” is rendered “fierce anger,” and “put him to shame” as “dishonored him.”
“The appointed time of David” is rendered “the appointment with David.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB has “arrow” where the Hebrew written text has “arrows.”
“Until David did great things” is rendered “but David more”; the meaning is uncertain.
MT 20:42–21:1. “To peace” is rendered “in safety,” and NASB supplies “to each other.”
